en: Mayon Volcano in Albay province features a nearly perfect cone shape and is the most active volcano in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through Cagayan Valley into the Pacific Ocean.
The Philippine tarsier, native to Bohol, possesses enormous eyes that are actually larger than its brain to aid nighttime hunting.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest peak in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of exactly 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Philippines supplies most of the world's abaca, a banana plant whose exceptionally strong fibers are used to make ropes and paper.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, situated between the provinces of Laguna and Rizal on Luzon island.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea protects over six hundred species of fish and three hundred coral species.
The amihan is the cool northeast monsoon that brings dry weather to the Philippines between November and February every year.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
Batanes is the northernmost province of the Philippines, consisting of ten volcanic islands bordering the Pacific Ocean and the West Philippine Sea.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is one of the largest forest eagles in the world and primarily hunts flying lemurs.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over one thousand symmetrical limestone mounds that turn cocoa-brown during the dry season.
